description: The average number of orders per account counts only accounts that have orders.

a.request: For each account with standing orders (`order.account_id`), count its orders. Work out the average number of orders per account, using only accounts that have at least one order. Keep the accounts whose order count is above that average. For each, show the account id, its order count, how far the count is above that average, and how far the count is above the average order count of the kept above-average accounts. Sort by this last difference from largest to smallest and return only the first 10 rows. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM "order" GROUP BY account_id), avg1 AS (SELECT AVG(order_count * 1.0) AS avg_all FROM counts), kept AS (SELECT c.account_id, c.order_count, c.order_count - a.avg_all AS diff_from_avg FROM counts c, avg1 a WHERE c.order_count > a.avg_all), avg2 AS (SELECT AVG(order_count * 1.0) AS avg_kept FROM kept) SELECT k.account_id, k.order_count, k.diff_from_avg, k.order_count - a2.avg_kept AS diff_from_kept_avg FROM kept k, avg2 a2 ORDER BY diff_from_kept_avg DESC LIMIT 10

c.request: For each account with standing orders (`order.account_id`), count its orders. Which accounts have more orders than the average number of orders per account? For each, show the account id, its order count, how far the count is above that average, and how far the count is above the average order count of those above-average accounts. Sort by this last difference from largest to smallest and give only the first 10. Don't round anything. The average number of orders per account counts only accounts that have orders.
c.sql: WITH oc AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM "order" GROUP BY account_id), avg_all AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS a FROM oc), above AS (SELECT oc.account_id, oc.cnt FROM oc, avg_all WHERE oc.cnt > avg_all.a), avg_above AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS b FROM above) SELECT above.account_id, above.cnt AS order_count, above.cnt - avg_all.a AS diff_from_avg, above.cnt - avg_above.b AS diff_from_above_avg FROM above, avg_all, avg_above ORDER BY diff_from_above_avg DESC LIMIT 10

b.request: Considering only accounts that have at least one order, compute each account's order count and the average order count per such account; keep accounts whose count exceeds that average; for each, output the account id, its count, count minus the overall average, and count minus the average count of the above-average accounts; sort by the last difference descending, take the top 10, with no rounding
b.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM `order` GROUP BY account_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_all FROM counts), above AS (SELECT c.account_id, c.cnt FROM counts c, overall o WHERE c.cnt > o.avg_all), above_avg AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_above FROM above) SELECT a.account_id, a.cnt AS order_count, a.cnt - o.avg_all AS diff_from_overall_avg, a.cnt - b.avg_above AS diff_from_above_avg FROM above a, overall o, above_avg b ORDER BY diff_from_above_avg DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: For each account that has at least one order (`order.account_id`), count its orders. The average number of orders per account is computed only over accounts that have orders, so accounts with no orders are excluded. Which of these accounts have more orders than that average? For each one, show the account id, its order count, how far the count is above that average, and how far the count is above the average order count of those above-average accounts. Sort by this last difference from largest to smallest, return only the first 10, and don't round anything.
d.sql: WITH oc AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM "order" GROUP BY account_id), avg_all AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS a FROM oc), above AS (SELECT oc.account_id, oc.cnt, oc.cnt - (SELECT a FROM avg_all) AS diff_overall FROM oc WHERE oc.cnt > (SELECT a FROM avg_all)), avg_above AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS a FROM above) SELECT account_id, cnt AS order_count, diff_overall AS above_overall_average, cnt - (SELECT a FROM avg_above) AS above_average_of_above FROM above ORDER BY above_average_of_above DESC LIMIT 10
